summary: Patch-level security bump of next from 15.5.23 to 15.5.24 in the workspace 'security' catalog, with the workspace override raised from next@<15.5.18 -> ~15.5.18 to next@<15.5.24 -> ~15.5.24 (GHSA-2xp9-vwfh-vxw4 / CVE-2026-75604 per the commit). The lockfile is regenerated consistently (no 15.5.23 references remain). next is only a devDependency of @cipherstash/nextjs (whose published peer range ^14 || ^15 is unchanged and which is not bundled) and an optional peer of evlog, a runtime dependency of @cipherstash/stack. Catalogs and overrides do not ship to consumers, so no published contract changes; the effect is confined to the next version this repo builds and tests against. The only scenario is a patch-level change in next/server or next/headers breaking @cipherstash/nextjs build/tests, which would be loud in CI. CI results were not available.

behaviour_changes.description: Workspace security catalog pins next to 15.5.24 (was 15.5.23); the @cipherstash/nextjs devDependency and evlog's optional next peer now resolve to 15.5.24, with matching @next/env and @next/swc-* platform binaries.

pnpm override for next raised to 'next@<15.5.24': '~15.5.24', forcing any workspace resolution of next below 15.5.24 to 15.5.x >= 15.5.24; pnpm also rewrites the next peer ranges of @clerk/nextjs and evlog in the lockfile to ~15.5.24. This affects installs of this workspace only, not consumers of published packages.

failure_scenarios.title: Patch-level next change breaks @cipherstash/nextjs build or tests
failure_scenarios.trigger: next 15.5.24 alters behaviour or types of next/server (NextResponse, NextRequest) or next/headers (cookies) used by @cipherstash/nextjs.
failure_scenarios.mechanism: packages/nextjs/src imports NextResponse/NextRequest from next/server and cookies from next/headers; its devDependency now resolves to 15.5.24. Security patches can tighten middleware/header handling.
failure_scenarios.consequence: Typecheck, build or vitest failures for @cipherstash/nextjs in CI (loud). Published artefacts are not affected because next is an external peer whose range is unchanged; customers choose their own next version.

evidence.claim: Security catalog sets next: 15.5.24 and the override is 'next@<15.5.24': '~15.5.24' with an advisory comment.
Lockfile replaces every next/@next/* 15.5.23 entry with 15.5.24 and updates rewritten peer ranges; git grep finds no 15.5.23 at head in pnpm-lock.yaml or pnpm-workspace.yaml.
next is a devDependency (catalog:security) and a peerDependency '^14 || ^15', unchanged by this diff.
Imports cookies from next/headers and NextRequest/NextResponse from next/server.
tsup config sets no noExternal, so next (a peer dependency) is left external by default.
Tests import NextResponse from next/server and mock next/headers; suites cover getCtsToken, resetCtsToken and protectMiddleware.
packages/stack depends on evlog 1.11.0, resolved with next@15.5.24 as its peer.
